author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Capture a minimal PCSX2 GS dump for a rendering report
summary: Reproduce a graphics fault on desktop PCSX2, capture only the necessary GS command window, replay it locally, record renderer and serial metadata, and share no disc image, firmware, or unrelated gameplay.
heroAlt: PCSX2 Tools menu with the command used to save a single-frame GS dump

sourceLabels.pcsx2-runner: Official dump replay and comparison tooling

blocks.text: Move the fault to a replayable desktop checkpoint

A GS dump records graphics commands and related GS state so developers can replay a visual problem without receiving the original disc image or save. Reproduce the same fault in a supported desktop PCSX2 build first. Choose a checkpoint where the broken frame appears quickly and where no unrelated cutscene or personal overlay needs to be captured.
A GS dump is not automatically safe to publish without review. Keep it private until it replays correctly and you have followed the target project's reporting and content rules.

items: A personally controlled disc image kept outside the report package.
Exact game serial, region, revision, PCSX2 build, renderer, and driver details.
A normal in-game save immediately before the visual fault.
A clean profile that reproduces the issue without unrelated cheats.
Enough private storage for the dump and one replay verification.

blocks.text: Capture, stop, and replay the smallest useful window

items: 1. Cold-boot the desktop title and navigate to the checkpoint using the documented clean profile.
2. Open the PCSX2 Tools action for saving a single-frame GS dump when one frame is sufficient.
3. For a multi-frame fault, begin capture immediately before it appears and stop as soon as the necessary transition completes.
4. Locate the dump in the documented snaps or data directory and record its byte size and SHA-256.
5. Close the game and replay the dump locally with the intended renderer.
6. Confirm that replay shows the same missing, misplaced, or blended graphics fault.
7. Repeat replay on a software or alternate renderer when that comparison is relevant.
8. Package only the dump, minimal settings, log, hashes, and reproduction notes permitted by the issue tracker.

blocks.text: A short reproducible dump lets graphics developers inspect draw order, targets, blending, and renderer differences without navigating the complete game. Single-frame capture is best for a static fault; a carefully bounded multi-frame dump is necessary only when previous framebuffer history or a transition creates the symptom.
Do not submit until the artifact independently reproduces the intended fault.

items: Local replay reaches the same broken frame without the original disc image.
The dump begins close to the fault and contains no long unrelated sequence.
Renderer, build, driver, serial, and clean settings are documented.
SHA-256 identifies the exact reviewed artifact.
The report contains no BIOS, game image, memory card, account token, or private path.
Replay is visually correct: capture closer to the failing frame or include required history.
The file grows through unrelated gameplay: stop and make a shorter artifact.
Only an emulator save state reproduces the issue: rebuild from an in-game save.
The dump includes material the target project will not accept: keep it private and ask for guidance.

blocks.text: Remove local reporting artifacts after verification

Keep the private original until the report is accepted, then remove surplus failed dumps and temporary logs from the snaps directory. Do not delete the in-game save or clean profile needed to reproduce a follow-up capture.
EmuCoreX and PCSX2 builds are different environments

A mobile fault that cannot be reproduced on desktop may require an EmuCoreX-specific renderer log instead. Do not claim a PCSX2 GS dump represents the Android bug unless the replay visibly preserves it.
Follow the official GS dump capture guide
